intro.text:
The studio is the same as every Tuesday — foam panels, a coffee going cold, the hiss of the desk fan. You've been doing this shift for four years. Nobody calls between two and three. That's why you took it.

Tonight, someone does.

open_phones.text:
You announce the lines and let the silence do the work. The first two calls are nothing — a hang-up and a wrong number. You're halfway through your cold coffee when Line 3 lights up.

You answer. The voice on the other end is calm. Unhurried.

'Good evening. I was hoping to reach—' a pause, '—you.' Not your on-air name. Your name. Your full name.

overlays.text: Nobody calls between two and three.

choices.label: Stay on the line. Keep them talking.

engage.text:
The voice continues as if it expected you to stay.

'Same way Nora did,' they say. 'She called this line every Tuesday for a year before you even started working here.'

Nora. Your sister. Dead three years. Nobody calls her Nora anymore — that was the family name, the private one. Her friends called her something else entirely.

'Who is this?' Your hand is on the disconnect button.

choices.label: Trace the call while keeping them talking.

cut_call.text:
You cut the line. The light on the desk goes dark.

For eleven seconds, nothing.

Then Line 5 lights up. The line you never give out.

choices.label: Leave it. Log it. End the show early.

insets.text: RESULT: DISCONNECTED  —  REGISTERED: N. [REDACTED]  —  DEACTIVATED: 3 YRS AGO

trace_result.text:
The trace takes twenty seconds. The number belongs to a deactivated account. You know the name before the screen finishes rendering it.

Your sister's account. Disconnected the month after the funeral.

They're still on the line. You can hear them breathing.

overlays.text: She called this line every Tuesday for a year.

choices.label: Put them on air. Let someone else hear this.

insets.text: TRACE ACTIVE  —  LINE 3  —  REGISTERED: N. [REDACTED]  —  DEACTIVATED ACCOUNT

the_address.text:
'I only want to give you something she left. There's an address — you already know the street. The house with the blue door. She said you'd come if someone asked the right way.'

A pause.

'This is the right way.'

overlays.text: Nora. The private name. Nobody called her that.
That number has been disconnected for three years.

choices.label: Put them on air. Let someone else hear this.
Cut the line and go home.

ending_follow.text:
You tell the overnight desk you're ending early. Technical difficulties.

The street is a twelve-minute drive. You know it — you grew up there. The house with the blue door is your childhood home. Your parents haven't lived there in eight years.

The light in the front room is on.

ending_broadcast.text:
You flip the switch. They're on air — broadcast to everyone still awake at 2am.

'Go ahead,' you say evenly. 'You were saying something about an address.'

Silence. Then the line goes dead.

You file a report in the morning. The number is traced to a deactivated account, origin unknown. The case is closed the same week.

You still do the Tuesday shift. Nobody calls between two and three.

overlays.text: She called this line every Tuesday.

ending_walk_away.text:
You log the call — time, duration, content — and leave the sheet on the overnight manager's desk on your way out.

The drive home is quiet. You sit in the car outside your flat for a while before going in.

You don't call anyone. There's no one to call.
